case_name: Abdul Nasar Adam Ismail Through Abdul Basheer Adam Ismail v The State Of Maharashtra & Ors.
petitioner: Abdul Nasar Adam Ismail Through Abdul Basheer Adam Ismail
facts: The appellant challenged a judgment and order dated 23/01/2013 passed by the Division Bench of the Bombay High Court dismissing his writ petition filed against an order of detention dated 16/4/2012 issued by the Principal Secretary (Appeals and Security), Government of Maharashtra, Home Department under the provisions of S. 3(1) of the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974.
The appellant was detained with a view to preventing him in future from smuggling goods.
The order of detention directed his detention with a view to preventing him in future from smuggling goods.
The detenu's statements u/s. 108 of the Customs Act, 1962 were recorded.
On perusal of the proposal and accompanying documents sent by the sponsoring authority, the detaining authority passed the aforementioned detention order.
issues: Whether the detention order is liable to be set aside if the detaining authority does not consider the detenu's representation independently?
Whether there was an unexplained delay in considering the representation of the detenu?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant assailed the detention order on two counts.
Firstly, he contended that the detenu through his lawyer submitted his representation dated 23/6/2012 to the jail authority for forwarding it to the State Government.
Counsel submitted that thus there is an inordinate delay in considering the representation of the detenu which has violated his right u/art. 22(5) of the Constitution of India.
Counsel submitted that there is delay at every stage, which indicates the casual approach of the State Government.
respondent_arguments: Mr. Arun R. Pednekar, learned counsel for the State of Maharashtra, on the other hand, submitted that the representation has been considered with utmost promptitude and the explanation offered by the State is reasonable and satisfactory.
Counsel submitted that if the delay is properly explained, there is no breach of the Constitutional imperative.
court_reasoning: We must make it clear that these were the only points urged by learned counsel for the detenu in this Court.
While closing the hearing, we directed learned counsel to submit a list of authorities on the above points urged by him.
Learned counsel for the State was to submit his reply to the above points.
holding: The appeal deserves to be dismissed.
